title: DVR Labs Playful 404 - Numbers Hanging on Threads

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: Characters hung from threads like a shop sign: they sway in a breeze, swing when pushed, and a thread pulled too far snaps, dropping the character.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: Each '404' digit is a damped pendulum on a stiff, slightly elastic SVG thread (paths sag when slack), simulated two substeps per frame on one rAF loop that pauses off-screen; simplex-noise breeze keeps them swaying; pointer velocity pushes them. Pulling a digit past thread length snaps it - it falls with throw physics, bounces, rolls flat on the shelf above the copy, and is re-hung seconds later.

design_tokens.borders: Thread rendered as 1-2px SVG strokes with sag curves; digits as solid heavy glyphs, no decorative borders
design_tokens.elevation: Flat page; depth implied only by swing amplitude and thread sag
design_tokens.typography: Oversized display digits as physical objects; compact functional type for search and recovery actions

interactive_mechanics: Sweeping pointer pushes hanging digits proportionally to cursor speed
Drag to swing; over-stretch snaps the thread with fall/bounce/roll physics
Snapped digit auto re-hangs after a delay or instantly via replay button
Beneath: real search combobox with suggestions and a way home
usability_notes: Error pages are the safest sandbox for physics metaphors - nothing transactional is at stake, so delight is pure win. The pattern still works because the functional layer (search + home link) stays fully independent of the toy. Must honor prefers-reduced-motion (digits simply hang), pause the rAF loop off-screen, and keep the digits decorative only (aria-hidden). Same-author sibling to ref-005 (DVR Labs).
